title: Ephemeral sticky routing for zero-loss cutover
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Deliver an edge/gateway routing mechanism that preserves in-flight sessions and streaming state during active-active regional traffic shifts. The feature (ephemeral sticky routing) issues a short-lived session lease at the ingress layer that pins traffic to a specific regional replica for the duration of a streaming session or critical multi-request transaction. On cutover, leases are transferred or drained with connection-preserving handshakes so we avoid application-visible reconnects. This ticket covers SLO definitions, circuit-breaker integration, load-shedding interaction, implementation of the ephemeral lease protocol, and staged rollout via feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming continuity: under simulated regional cutover, >=99.5% of active streaming sessions complete without application-level reconnects (measured for sessions with <30s idle windows)
SLO preservation: 99.95% success rate for short-form (<=128 tokens) text-gen requests during cutover windows against control baseline
Failover latency: 95th percentile additional latency introduced by lease transfer <=200ms
Load-shedding coherence: when overloaded, system sheds load according to configured weights without violating session pinning for canary traffic
Circuit-breaker hooks: routing respects upstream circuit breakers and falls back to hedged requests where appropriate
Observability: per-lease telemetry (create/renew/transfer/drain) appears on Console with dashboards and alerts
Rollback safety: feature flag off returns to stateless routing with documented behavior and no residual leases
design_notes: Lease token: TTL-based opaque token stored in fast edge KV (local node + async cross-region replicate). Designed for ephemeral lifetime (default 30s) and renewals on activity.
Pinning policy: streaming and multi-request sessions automatically request a lease; single-shot stateless calls skip pinning to maximize multiplexing and batching efficiency.
Transfer strategy: two-phase transfer during handoff - (1) advertise incoming drain window to new region, (2) handshake to flush client KV/stream pointers and confirm transfer before cutting route.

Consistency vs availability trade-off: soft guarantees (best-effort transfer) chosen over strict synchronous KV replication to avoid cross-region tail latency spikes. Compensate with hedged requests and short-term request duplication prevention ids.

Circuit breaker integration: routing consults regional health matrix and circuit state; if a region is flagged degraded, leases are not granted and existing leases are opportunistically drained to healthy regions.

Load-shedding interaction: implement per-lease priority labels so shedder can prefer dropping new, non-pinned workloads first. Pinned sessions still subject to shedding under emergency thresholds but with gentler ramp-downs.
Security: lease tokens encrypted at rest in edge KV; tokens bound to client connection fingerprint to reduce hijack surface.
Operational: provide a diagnostic endpoint to list active leases per customer and per route for support troubleshooting
implementation_plan: Prototype lease token lifecycle in sandbox edge cluster (feature-branch: feature/ephemeral-lease-proto)
Add edge KV schema and background async replicator with eventual cross-region visibility
Implement handshake protocol in streaming proxy and HTTP gateway components
Wire circuit-breaker and load-shed hooks to routing decision path
Add observability: lease metrics, tracing spans, and Console dashboard widgets
Run chaos experiments simulating region drain and network partitions
Gradual rollout: internal canary -> 10% customer traffic -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
Finalize docs: runbook, Confluence architecture doc, and support playbook
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept for lease token creation and local KV storage validated in lab cluster. Affects edge proxy and local KV client.
2026-02-26: Design review with PM/RE/Platform. Agreed on 30s default TTL and two-phase transfer. PM requested explicit metrics for user-visible reconnect rate.
2026-03-03: Prototype PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/413). Basic handshake implemented; tests added for token binding to connection fingerprint.

2026-03-06: Load test (k6) with synthetic streaming sessions under rolling cutover. Observed 0.8% reconnects at 10k RPS; root cause: rare race in transfer confirmation. Mitigation: add confirmation ack and retry path.
2026-03-10: Added circuit-breaker consult to routing path. Still pending cross-region replicator and Console panels. Scheduling chaos experiments for 2026-03-15.
Outstanding: KV async replicator, formal SLO gating in release pipeline, support playbook write-up
risks_mitigation: Race conditions during transfer: mitigate with idempotent transfer tokens and explicit confirmation acks
Increased tail latency from cross-region sync: avoid synchronous waits; prefer async replication and hedging where needed
Operational complexity: keep feature behind flag and build tooling to inspect/evict leases
Security token theft: bind tokens to connection metadata and rotate TTL aggressively
Unexpected load amplification from hedging: cap parallel hedges per-client and per-route
qa_checklist: Functional: create/renew/transfer/drain flows work under lab conditions
Stress: 50k concurrent streaming sessions, initiate region drain, measure reconnect rate
Chaos: simulate cross-region partition, ensure fallback hedging behaves within SLOs
Security: token replay attempts rejected and audited
Observability: Console shows per-customer lease counts and transfer latencies
Feature flag: toggling disables lease logic without leaving orphaned state
notes: PM feedback: surface an opt-out for customers who want pure stateless low-latency routing
Design/RE: agree to surface an SLO-based auto-rollout gate; if reconnect rate >0.7% during canary, auto-roll back
Infra: KV replicator will use a best-effort Batcher to limit metadata write amplification
Support asked for API to manually evict leases for emergency evacuations (implemented as admin-only endpoint)
Next step: pre-schedule a business-hours canary and notify on-call + support
